idiom_name: object literal typed as the collaborator interface (satisfies)
implementation_notes: TypeScript's realization is still the local idiom - an object literal with the canned answers - but the compiler makes the contract explicit: declare the collaborator as an interface, then write the stub as const warehouse: Pick<Warehouse, 'hasInventory'> = { hasInventory: () => false } (or annotate the full interface, or use satisfies) so a signature drift is a type error rather than a runtime surprise. Because TypeScript is structurally typed, any object with the right members is accepted where the interface is expected, which is exactly what makes a hand-written literal a first-class stub; where the double must satisfy the whole interface, jest.fn<T>()/vi.fn<T>() plus jest.mocked/vi.mocked supply typed canned answers and let the test assert only the members it uses. Casting a partial object through as unknown as Warehouse gives up the checking that makes this idiom worthwhile.
pitfalls: `as unknown as Warehouse` on a partial object removes the check that the stub matches the collaborator; use a complete literal or jest.mocked so the compiler keeps working.
jest.fn() without a type parameter yields `any`-typed returns; use jest.fn<() => boolean>() or jest.mocked(obj.method) so the canned answer is checked.
Structural typing accepts a shape-compatible object where a class with private fields or a brand is required; inject at the interface-typed seam, not the concrete-class seam.

variants.name: Typed jest.fn<T>()/vi.fn<T>() or jest.mocked/vi.mocked
variants.implementation_notes: When the suite runs on Jest or Vitest, the typed canned answer is jest.fn<() => boolean>().mockReturnValue(false) or vi.mocked(example.add).mockReturnValue(10) after the module has been mocked; mockResolvedValue/mockRejectedValue cover async collaborators and mockReturnValueOnce sequences cover consecutive calls. The type parameter (or jest.mocked, which preserves the original signature) keeps the answer checked against the collaborator, which is the part a plain object literal gives up when the interface is wide. Configure before injection, and reset in teardown (mockRestore, restoreAllMocks, vi.resetAllMocks) because a leaked answer fails a later test for the wrong reason.
pitfalls: vi.mocked is a type helper only: it checks types but mocks nothing, so the module or function must already be a mock (vi.mock) or the real implementation still runs.
mockReturnValueOnce values are consumed in order and further calls fall back to mockReturnValue or return undefined.
A typed jest.fn() records calls too; asserting on them turns the stub into an interaction test, so keep the assertion style deliberate.
